note: Icon packs from open repositories, each under its own license (see the LICENSE.txt and ATTRIBUTION.md of each folder), not under the MIT license of SiliCoDraw. Written by dev/icon-import/install.ps1.

packs.name: Expression Atlas anatomograms
packs.by: EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI): the anatomograms its Expression Atlas uses to show the organs and tissues of experiments
packs.credit: Anatomograms from Expression Atlas, EMBL-EBI (Expression Atlas in 2026, Nucleic Acids Research, doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1238), CC BY 4.0, adapted
packs.plain: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0): you may use, change and share these drawings, also commercially, as long as you give credit, link to the license and say that you changed them. The repository's README puts all its images under CC BY 4.0 (its code is Apache 2.0), and the Expression Atlas licence page applies CC BY 4.0 to all copyrightable material of the site, naming the species anatomograms. The outline of the male human body comes from a public-domain drawing on Wikimedia Commons (by Vsion, SVG by Sjef, text by tsaitgaist), named in that icon's credits. This pack is not endorsed by EMBL-EBI.
packs.ask: This means that anyone is free to copy, reuse, display and distribute the images and information on our database, provided you give us credit by citing: Expression Atlas in 2026: enabling FAIR and open expression data through community collaboration and integration (Nucleic Acids Research, 10 December 2025).
packs.how: Cite the Expression Atlas article, as EMBL-EBI asks: Expression Atlas in 2026: enabling FAIR and open expression data through community collaboration and integration (Nucleic Acids Research, 10 December 2025, doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1238). SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you: Anatomograms from Expression Atlas, EMBL-EBI (Expression Atlas in 2026, Nucleic Acids Research, doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1238), CC BY 4.0, adapted. Put the full citation in the reference list or the acknowledgments too.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format, one icon per anatomogram: the small EBI attribution logo (a link to the licence page) taken out; the tissue shapes, which the files leave invisible for the Expression Atlas web page to color, filled with one light red under the outline so that the organs show; tissues that spread over the whole body (skin, skeletal muscle, fat, bone, cartilage, bone marrow, blood vessels, nerves, lymph nodes and the like) left unfilled, and a tissue drawn twice under two ontology ids filled once; fitted into a 100 × 100 box, styles written out as attributes, metadata removed, coordinates rounded, and the outline and tissue colors made recolorable (the green anole's tissues are too small a part of it for a color field of their own: they change with their color group). Each icon was drawn and compared with the adapted drawing on a white and on a dark page. Names are SiliCoDraw's (common name and species); the tissues each drawing shows are its search words. Left out: three drawings over 700 KB each because of their fine line work (the potato plant, the whole Brachypodium plant and the sorghum flower parts).

packs.name: Arcadia Science
packs.by: Arcadia Science, Free organism illustration library (contributors Audrey Bell, Megan Hochstrasser, Robert Roth and Greg Wright)
packs.credit: Arcadia Science, Free organism illustration library (doi:10.5281/zenodo.18395998), CC0
packs.plain: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): Arcadia Science gave up its copyright in these illustrations, so you may use, change and share them for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. Ten of the drawings were adapted by Arcadia Science from PhyloPic silhouettes that are public domain or CC0 there; their tooltips and credits name the PhyloPic uploader, as the library does.
packs.ask: All images are released under CC0, which has no usage restrictions. That said, feel free to cite the associated pub, "A free, open-access library of high-quality organism illustrations for science communication," to help others find this resource.
packs.how: No credit is required. A citation is appreciated: Bell A, Hochstrasser ML, Roth R, Wright G (2025). A free, open-access library of high-quality organism illustrations for science communication. The Stacks. doi:10.57844/arcadia-4gbv-pzkv. SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these icons by itself; Page → Copy full icon credits lists each icon with the library's DOI.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: each organism as its three-color drawing and as its silhouette (the library's PNG pictures and animations are not included), fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, a small soft shadow drawn with an embedded picture removed from the mouse (it barely shows), coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable. Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page.
packs.each: {n} by {by}. Free organism illustration library, version 1.2. https://doi.org/{doi}

packs.name: BioDraws
packs.credit: Images are obtained from BioDraws.com (CC BY-SA 4.0), adapted
packs.plain: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0): you may use, change and share the illustrations, also commercially, as long as you give credit, link to the license, say that changes were made, and share what you make from them under the same license.
packs.ask: If you have used illustrations from our website for your thesis, presentations, publications, or posters, please cite us by mentioning “Images are obtained from BioDraws.com.” in the figure legend.
packs.shareAlikeText: BioDraws' terms say: “If you remix, transform, or build upon the material, you must distribute your contributions under the same license as the original.” Changed icons must therefore stay under CC BY-SA 4.0, and this can extend to a figure you build with them. Many journals publish under other licenses: check your journal's terms before you use these icons in a paper.
packs.how: Put the credit in the figure legend or on the figure: Images are obtained from BioDraws.com (CC BY-SA 4.0), adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: fitted into a 100 × 100 box, styles written out as attributes, text and editor data removed, coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable. The converted icons remain under CC BY-SA 4.0.

packs.name: Bioicons
packs.by: Bioicons, a free community library of scientific icons curated by Simon Dürr; every icon names its creator and its license
packs.license: CC0 / CC BY 4.0 / CC BY-SA 4.0 / MIT, per icon
packs.mixedShare: about two in five of them: those under CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or MIT
packs.credit: Bioicons (bioicons.com), CC BY 4.0 / CC BY-SA 4.0 / MIT per icon, adapted
packs.plain: Each icon is under the license its creator chose, as the folder Bioicons files it in says: CC0 (public domain: no credit needed), Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0: you may use, change and share it, also commercially, as long as you credit the creator, link to the license and say that you changed it), Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0: the same, and what you make from the icon must be shared under the same license) or MIT (use it freely, keeping the creator's copyright and license notice). An icon's tooltip names its creator and license. This pack is not endorsed by Bioicons or by the creators.
packs.ask: Please always cite the individual icons and their respective license. Credit to the platform itself is appreciated but not necessary.
packs.how: Credit every icon under CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or MIT with its name, its creator and its license, and say that it was adapted, for example: Neutrophil by Helicase 11, bioicons.com, CC BY 4.0, adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you and keeps it up to date. With more than three such icons the line names only Bioicons: then paste Copy full icon credits into the figure legend or the acknowledgments. Icons under CC0 need no credit.
packs.shareAlikeText: Some icons of this pack (26 of them; their tooltip says CC BY-SA 4.0) are share-alike. Their license says that when you share adapted material you produce, “The Adapter's License You apply must be a Creative Commons license with the same License Elements, this version or later, or a BY-SA Compatible License” (section 3(b)). A changed icon must therefore stay under CC BY-SA, and this can extend to a figure you build with it. Many journals publish under other licenses: check your journal's terms before you use these icons in a paper. The other icons of this pack are not share-alike.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, small text labels, metadata and editor data removed, embedded pictures that barely show removed, the white page of drawings traced from a picture removed, coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable (every icon can be recolored by its color groups). Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. Icons that are only another color of a kept one are left out; their names still find it.

packs.name: Inkscape Electric Symbols
packs.by: the Power Electronics and Electrical Drives group (LEA) of Paderborn University, which publishes them as its Inkscape Electric Symbols library
packs.credit: Inkscape Electric Symbols, Paderborn University LEA (github.com/upb-lea/Inkscape_electric_Symbols), CC0 1.0
packs.plain: Public domain, dedicated under Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): you may copy, change and share these symbols for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. The repository's LICENSE is the CC0 1.0 legal code, and the symbol sheet's own metadata names CC0 1.0. This pack is not endorsed by Paderborn University or its LEA group.
packs.how: No credit is required, and SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these symbols. The repository asks for none; if you want to mention the library, Page → Copy full icon credits gives a line for it.
packs.changes: Taken out of the repository's one SVG sheet (Inkscape_Symbols_All.svg) one drawing at a time and converted to SiliCoDraw's icon format: arrowheads (SVG markers) drawn as shapes of their own, the letters and signs inside a symbol (V, A, M, G, +, −, &, ≥1, abc/dq, LUT, MUX and the like) set as outlines in MathJax's sans-serif face instead of the sheet's live text, the placeholder ratio of the transformers (n:1) left out, fitted into a 100 × 100 box, coordinates rounded and the colors made recolorable (the line color is Color 1). Each icon was drawn and compared with what it was converted from on a white and on a dark page. Names and groups are SiliCoDraw's, based on the titles the sheet gives its symbols. Left out: symbols the sheet has again in another size, turned or drawn a second time, plain symbols framed as blocks, a USB plug that carries the USB trident logo, and the sheet's example circuits, labels and instructions.

packs.name: Health Icons
packs.by: Health Icons, a volunteer project hosted by the public-health not-for-profit Resolve to Save Lives (maintainers Daniel Burka and Jahanvi Singh, with volunteer contributors)
packs.plain: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): the makers of Health Icons waived all copyright in these icons, so you may use, change and share them for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. The repository's LICENSE puts the icon files in the public domain under CC0; its MIT license covers only the code of the healthicons.org website. This pack is not endorsed by Health Icons or Resolve to Save Lives.
packs.ask: The icons are in the public domain, so you can use them in any type of project, for free, with no credit needed.
packs.how: No credit is required, and SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these icons. If you want to mention the library, Page → Copy full icon credits gives a line for it.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format, one style only (the 48 px filled icons; the outline style and the 24 px versions draw the same subjects): fitted into a 100 × 100 box, coordinates rounded, and the color made recolorable (the icons are drawn in one color). Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. Left out: letters, digits and currency signs, plain geometric shapes, logos and trademarks, user-interface symbols (menus, zoom and settings buttons, signal bars, check marks and question marks) and a military vehicle.

packs.name: NIH BioArt Source
packs.by: NIH BioArt Source of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), U.S. National Institutes of Health; every entry names its creator
packs.plain: Only entries that the site labels “Public Domain” are in this pack. Its terms say they are free for any use, including commercial use. The site gives no legal text beyond its terms page, and it expects users to respect the integrity and intended use of the illustrations. This pack is not endorsed by NIH or NIAID.
packs.ask: If the entry is licensed as "Public Domain" citation is appreciated but not required (See "How to Cite Entries in NIH BioArt Source").
packs.how: No credit is required. A credit is appreciated: “Illustration from NIAID NIH BioArt Source (bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/###)”, with the entry's number (an icon's tooltip and Copy full icon credits give it). SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these icons by itself.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: one icon per drawing (the site's other color versions of the same drawing are left out, since SiliCoDraw recolors icons), fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, color inversions of masks written into the colors, drop shadows, glows and pattern fills kept, text, editor data and embedded pictures that barely show removed (each icon is checked against the original on a white and on a dark page), coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable.
packs.each: {n} by {by}: Illustration from NIAID NIH BioArt Source ({page})

packs.name: OCHA Humanitarian Icons
packs.by: the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), which publishes them as its Humanitarian Icons
packs.plain: Public domain, dedicated under Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): you may copy, change and share these icons for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. The repository's LICENSE is the CC0 1.0 legal code. OCHA says it does not intend an official meaning for the icons and that their meaning and representation do not imply acceptance or endorsement by the United Nations; this pack is not endorsed by OCHA or the United Nations, and it contains no UN emblem.
packs.ask: While attribution is not required, we would appreciate: Crediting OCHA where feasible.
packs.how: No credit is required, and SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these icons. OCHA appreciates a credit where feasible (Page → Copy full icon credits gives a line for it) and, for its records, an email to ochavisual@un.org with a link to your webpage or publication; both are up to you.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format, one color version only (black; the UN-blue and white files are the same drawings, and SiliCoDraw recolors icons): fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, coordinates rounded, and the color made recolorable. Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. Names are the file names in words, in American spelling. The groups are SiliCoDraw's, since the repository has none. Left out: user-interface and file-type symbols, the plain status marks, icons whose meaning is lettering (NGO, NFI), icons of conflict, violence and the military, religious buildings, and the icons with UN lettering.

packs.name: Open Crop Icons
packs.by: the contributors of Open Crop Icons, an icon set of the OpenFarm project
packs.credit: Open Crop Icons, OpenFarm contributors (github.com/openfarmcc/open-crop-icons), CC0 1.0
packs.plain: Public domain, dedicated under Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): you may copy, change and share these icons for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. The repository's README releases the icons under CC0 and its package.json declares CC0-1.0. The repository names no creator per icon. This pack is not endorsed by OpenFarm or the icons' contributors.
packs.ask: These are released under a CC0 license. They're public domain works so use them without restriction. A credit somewhere to help other people find them would be in good spirit, but is not required.
packs.how: No credit is required, and SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these icons. The makers would welcome a credit somewhere to help other people find the icons: Page → Copy full icon credits gives a line for it, if you want to give one.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format, one drawing per crop (the PNG pictures and the 24, 32 and 64 px copies of a few icons are not included): fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable. Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. Names are the folder names in words, with misspellings corrected (Artichoke, Marjoram, Chanterelle, Portobello, Brussels Sprout, Lacinato Kale, Yukon Gold Potato and others); the groups are SiliCoDraw's, since the repository has none. Left out: the cannabis plant and the psilocybin mushroom; drawings that are only another color of a drawing kept (the purple, red, white and yellow carrots, the red cabbage, the white and yellow onions, the purple-pod and wax beans, the red and rainbow chards, the black habanero, the Granny Smith apple and others: SiliCoDraw recolors icons, and their names still find the drawing kept); and the cantaloupe, whose conversion did not match the original. A drawing of another ripeness or species is an icon of its own, even where only its colors differ (the green, red, orange and yellow bell peppers, the oyster mushrooms, the nectarine beside the peach).

packs.name: PhyloPic
packs.by: PhyloPic, a free database of organism silhouettes created by T. Michael Keesey, with images uploaded by many contributors; every silhouette names its creator and its license
packs.license: Public domain / CC0 / CC BY 3.0 / CC BY 4.0, per icon
packs.mixedShare: about one in five of them: those under CC BY 3.0 or CC BY 4.0
packs.credit: PhyloPic (phylopic.org), CC BY 3.0 / CC BY 4.0 per icon, adapted
packs.plain: Each silhouette is under the license its uploader chose on PhyloPic, as the image's own record states: the Public Domain Mark or CC0 (public domain: use it anywhere, in any way, without credit) or Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 or 4.0 (CC BY: you may use, change and share it, also commercially, as long as you credit its creator, link to the license and say that you changed it). Silhouettes under NonCommercial or ShareAlike licenses are not in this pack. An icon's tooltip names its creator and license. This pack is not endorsed by PhyloPic or by the creators.
packs.ask: Images under a Creative Commons Attribution Deed (CC-BY 3.0 or CC-BY 4.0) must be credited to the creator(s). The attribution text can be found on Image Pages. You must also provide a link to the license. And, if you have made any significant changes to the images, you must indicate what they are. Attributing images to PhyloPic is never required. (But mentioning the site is always appreciated!)
packs.how: Credit every silhouette under CC BY 3.0 or CC BY 4.0 with its taxon, its creator as PhyloPic names it and its license, and say that it was adapted, for example: Colinus virginianus by Edwin Price, phylopic.org, CC BY 4.0, adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you and keeps it up to date. With more than three such icons the line names only PhyloPic: then paste Copy full icon credits (each creator, image page and license with its link) into the figure legend or the acknowledgments. Silhouettes in the public domain or under CC0 need no credit; mentioning PhyloPic is appreciated.
packs.changes: Converted from PhyloPic's vector files (vector.svg: PhyloPic's own vector version of each silhouette, pure black) to SiliCoDraw's icon format: fitted into a 100 × 100 box, metadata removed, coordinates rounded, and the color made recolorable. Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. A selection: one silhouette per taxon and one per genus, spread over the tree of life (model organisms first), without human figures. Each icon is named by its taxon as PhyloPic names it, which the credits print; the common names PhyloPic lists for the taxon (in many languages) are search words.

packs.name: Reactome Icon Library
packs.by: Reactome, the open-source, curated pathway knowledgebase; every icon names its designer and the Reactome curator who checked it
packs.credit: Reactome Icon Library (reactome.org/icon-lib), CC BY 4.0, adapted
packs.plain: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0): you may use, change and share these icons, also commercially, as long as you give appropriate credit, link to the license and say that you changed them. Reactome's license agreement puts its Icon Library under this license; the GitHub repository the icons were taken from also carries an Apache License 2.0 file. This pack is not endorsed by Reactome.
packs.ask: User may copy, modify, and distribute these materials, provided that appropriate credit is given, a link to the license is included, and any modifications made by User are clearly indicated.
packs.how: Credit every icon you use with its name and designer, name the Reactome Icon Library and the license with its link, and say that it was adapted, for example: Neuron by Sam Norwitz, reactome.org/icon-lib, CC BY 4.0, adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you and keeps it up to date. With more than three such icons the line names only the Reactome Icon Library: then paste Copy full icon credits into the figure legend or the acknowledgments.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: fitted into a 100 × 100 box, ids renamed, coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable where the drawing has flat colors (every icon can be recolored by its color groups). Left out: the library's arrows and pathway background pictures, its label badges (proteins, compounds and drugs drawn as a pill, hexagon or tag with the name written in as outlines: SiliCoDraw makes such labels as real text), and drawings that are only other colors of one another (sugar symbols drawn alike, genes drawn as one DNA strand with a colored band, the members of a transporter or receptor family drawn alike, plain shaded spheres); the names of those still find the drawing kept. A drawing whose color or detail tells what it is (a sugar such as lyxose or fructose, a nucleotide, a damaged base, a T cell subtype, a vesicle type) is an icon of its own. Each icon was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page.
packs.each: {n} by {by}. Reactome Icon Library, CC BY 4.0. {page}

packs.name: SBOL Visual
packs.by: the SBOL developers (the Synthetic Biology Open Language community, SynBioDex), whose SBOL Visual standard defines these glyphs for genetic designs, molecular species and their interactions
packs.credit: SBOL Visual glyphs, the SBOL developers (github.com/SynBioDex/SBOL-visual), CC0 1.0
packs.plain: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0): the SBOL developers waived all copyright in the SBOL Visual glyphs, so you may use, change and share them for any purpose, also commercially, without asking and without giving credit. The waiver is the exception in the repository's LICENSE.html, which puts the rest of the repository (the specification text, its examples and documents) under CC BY 4.0; this pack holds the glyphs only, taken from the GitHub repository (the sbolstandard.org website is under another license and was not used). This pack is not endorsed by the SBOL developers.
packs.ask: Exception: to the extent possible under law, the SBOL developers have waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to SBOL Visual glyphs.
packs.how: No credit is required (the SBOL developers ask for none), and SiliCoDraw adds no credit line for these glyphs. If you want to name the standard (useful when a figure follows it), Page → Copy full icon credits gives a line for it.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: each glyph fitted into a 100 × 100 box by what it draws (so the glyphs no longer share one scale or sit on their backbone line), style sheets written out as attributes, an arrowhead drawn as a marker written out as a shape, metadata removed, coordinates rounded, and the color made recolorable; the white fill of the single-stranded nucleic acid's open wave line, which showed as a white patch on a dark page, was taken off (the white interiors of Dissociation and of the Process node, which cover lines behind them, are kept). The characters some glyphs are made of (the ? of the replacement glyph, the brackets of No glyph assigned, the ellipsis of Omitted detail, the AAA of the polyA site, the asterisks of the stop sites) are set as outlines in another sans-serif face (MathJax's), since an icon holds no text; SBOL Visual leaves the face open. Each glyph was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. Names follow the glyph sets of the repository. Left out: the specification and example drawings, the Deprecated glyphs, and the glyphs that are copies of another one (the replacement glyph, the No glyph assigned brackets and the SBGN nucleic-acid shape appear in several glyph sets: each is in the pack once).

packs.name: SciDraw
packs.by: SciDraw, a community repository of scientific drawings; every drawing names its authors
packs.plain: Each drawing is under the license its author chose: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0: you may use, change and share it, also commercially, as long as you credit the author) or CC0 (public domain: no credit needed). An icon's tooltip names its license.
packs.ask: Please acknowledge the contribution of the image's authors and of SciDraw in the acknowledgements section of your work. You can use the DOI displayed below each drawing to cite the illustration properly.
packs.how: Credit every CC BY drawing you use with its authors and DOI, name SciDraw and the license, and say that it was adapted, for example: Mouse by A. Name (doi:10.5281/zenodo.0000000), scidraw.io, CC BY 4.0, adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you and keeps it up to date. With more than three such drawings the line names only SciDraw: then paste Copy full icon credits into the figure legend or the acknowledgments. Drawings under CC0 need no credit.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: fitted into a 100 × 100 box, style sheets written out as attributes, text and editor data removed, coordinates rounded, and the two main colors made recolorable.

packs.name: Servier Medical Art
packs.by: Servier Medical Art (SMART), the medical illustration bank of Servier
packs.credit: Images adapted from Servier Medical Art (https://smart.servier.com/), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
packs.plain: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0): you may use, change and share the images, also commercially, as long as you credit Servier Medical Art, link to the license and say that the images were changed. The credit must not suggest that Servier endorses you or your work. Servier's name and logo are not part of the license. The drawings keep Servier's shaded style (shading and highlights, not flat colors); changing the main color or the accent recolors their shades with them.
packs.ask: Image adapted from Servier Medical Art (https://smart.servier.com/), licensed under CC BY 4.0
packs.how: Put the credit in the figure legend or on the figure: Images adapted from Servier Medical Art (https://smart.servier.com/), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you.
packs.changes: Converted from Servier's PowerPoint kits (the drawings are vector shapes there) to SiliCoDraw's icon format: each drawing of a slide redrawn as SVG, fitted into a 100 × 100 box, text labels left out, coordinates rounded, very small invisible parts dropped, and the main color and accent made recolorable together with their shades. The converted icons remain under CC BY 4.0.

packs.name: WMO WorldWeatherSymbols
packs.by: the OGC Meteorology and Oceanography Domain Working Group (OGC MetOcean DWG), whose WorldWeatherSymbols draw the international weather symbols of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) with full metadata
packs.credit: WorldWeatherSymbols, OGC MetOcean DWG and WMO (github.com/OGCMetOceanDWG/WorldWeatherSymbols), CC BY 4.0, adapted
packs.plain: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0): you may use, change and share these symbols, also commercially, as long as you give credit, link to the license and say that you changed them. The repository's LICENSE.md releases it under CC BY 4.0, and every symbol's own metadata links CC BY 4.0 as its license (its rights field still names CC BY 3.0, from before the maintainers moved every file to 4.0 in 2022; both are attribution licenses). The symbols follow WMO-No. 485 and, for aviation, WMO-No. 49; this pack is not endorsed by the WMO, ICAO or the OGC.
packs.ask: Copyright (C) 2013-2021 OGC Meteorology and Oceanography Domain Working Group. This website is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
packs.how: The repository gives no wording of its own. Put this line in the figure legend or on the figure: WorldWeatherSymbols, OGC MetOcean DWG and WMO (github.com/OGCMetOceanDWG/WorldWeatherSymbols), CC BY 4.0, adapted. SiliCoDraw writes this line on the page for you.
packs.changes: Converted from SVG to SiliCoDraw's icon format: each symbol fitted into a 100 × 100 box by what it draws (so the symbols no longer share one scale), repeated parts and arrowheads written out as shapes, styles written out as attributes, metadata removed, coordinates rounded, and the color made recolorable. Each symbol was drawn and compared with the original on a white and on a dark page. A symbol drawn the same in several code tables (or as good as the same: a plain circle, the same glyph drawn a second time with a hair of difference) is in the pack once, under its first code (the other codes are search words). Stray dots left by the drawing program were taken out, and a symbol that runs off its own page (the automatic station triangle, the tropical cyclones) is shown whole. Names are the WMO code and its description, shortened, footnotes taken off and a few typos corrected; the ICAO symbols, which have no description, are named from their file names. Left out: the Southern Hemisphere wind arrows and tropical cyclones (mirror images of the Northern ones: flip the icon), the symbols whose meaning is a digit written as text, plain lines, and two files that draw nothing as published.
